subject: Deployment boundary & SLO qualification for Medivance - post-call recap
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@medivance.com>, Tom Hsu <t.hsu@medivance.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-11T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: isolation requirements + next steps

Hi Samantha / Tom,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good discussion. Quick recap and a few concrete asks so we can align on the right deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem).

Key constraints you shared (please confirm):
- P95 inference latency target: 150ms for patient-facing flows (priority)
- Peak QPS: 120 sustained, spikes to ~380 for nightly batch and claims ingest
- Data residency: US-only; some PHI in payloads
- Isolation tolerance: low — engineering wants strong tenancy boundaries; compliance is sensitive to cross-tenant blast radius

From a Redwood standpoint, the tradeoffs are:
- Hosted API: fastest to market and simplest ops; recommend prefix/KV isolation + tenant-level routing for most workloads but weaker physical isolation than Dedicated/Private
- Dedicated capacity: gives you GPU pools isolated to your account (recommended if you want bounded noisy-neighbor risk and predictable P99s)
- Private VPC/on-prem: necessary if your procurement or regulators require customer-managed networking or air-gapped hardware (longer lead time + infra ops on your side)

Open questions we need to size an accurate recommendation and pricing:  (please answer if you can)
1) Are all workflows (patient chat, claims enrichment, embedding index updates) considered equally sensitive, or can we tier them?
2) For the patient-facing flow we should confirm SLA tolerance: is 99.9% at P95 acceptable? Do you require latency-based SLOs per endpoint?
3) Do you expect model version pinning per environment (e.g., prod vs staging) or frequent releases that would require canary capacity?
4) Procurement timeline / preferred contract term (monthly, 12/24m)?

Next steps I propose:
- You: confirm answers to Q1–Q4 above and share a rough weekly token/embedding volume for production and nightly batch.
- Redwood: we’ll produce a short matrix (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) showing expected P95/P99, mitigations for noisy neighbors, and a suggested POC plan. I’ve attached a cribsheet and SLO template to make answers easier.
- Optional: schedule a 30-min technical POC kickoff next week to scope Dedicated capacity.

Attachments: deployment-options-cribsheet.pdf, medivance-slo-template.xlsx

Thanks — happy to jump on a call to walk through the matrix.

Best,
Priyom
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priyom@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0128

--

From: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@medivance.com>

Cc: Tom Hsu <t.hsu@medivance.com>
Date: 2027-10-11T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: isolation requirements + next steps

Priyom — thanks for the clear recap and the cribsheet. Quick answers below:

Q1: Patient-facing chat and claims enrichment are both sensitive; chat is slightly higher priority for latency. We cannot tier them by tenancy today.
Q2: 99.9% at P95 is our current target; for patient chat we'd prefer 99.95% if that changes the recommendation.
Q3: We will pin model versions for prod, but expect monthly cadence for model updates and plan small canaries.
Q4: Procurement prefers a 12–24 month term; procurement timeline is ~6 weeks after we pick architecture.

Also one more technical ask from our infra lead: what isolation guarantees do you provide for KV cache and prefix caching? We worry about cross-tenant cache leakage and request path amplification under noisy load.

I'll extract weekly volumes from analytics and drop them into the SLO template by COB tomorrow.

Thanks,
Samantha
Sr. Product Manager, AI | Medivance Health
samantha.cole@medivance.com | (617) 555-3344
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@medivance.com>
Date: 2027-10-12T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: isolation requirements + next steps — initial technical recommendation

Samantha / team — looping in a technical note based on the constraints you shared.

Short recommendation (technical):
- If Medivance requires P95 ~150ms with 99.95% for patient chat and low tolerance for blast radius, Dedicated capacity is the safest option. It provides:
  * GPU pools dedicated to your tenant (no co-tenancy on serving hosts)
  * Deterministic autoscaling policies and capacity reservations for nightly spikes
  * Per-tenant KV namespaces and enforced prefix isolation; cache eviction policies scoped to tenant KV to avoid cross-tenant amplification
- Hosted API can meet latency if we reserve burst/dedicated nodes and apply strict routing rules, but physical isolation is not guaranteed — we mitigate with quotas, per-tenant queues, and admission control. Good for fast time-to-prod if procurement/timelines are tight.
- Private VPC is recommended only if procurement/regulatory requires customer-managed networking or on-prem hardware (we've seen 6–10 week delivery time).

Follow-ups I need from the Medivance infra team to produce a sizing and POC plan:
- Typical request size distribution (tokens per request) for patient chat vs claims
- Batch throughput window (hours) and whether batches can be throttled or scheduled to off-peak
- Any hard requirements on model cache persistence across restarts (affects KV store choices)

I attached a quick pricing snapshot for Dedicated so procurement can see order-of-magnitude costs (redwood-dedicated-pricing.xlsx).

If you want, Monica and I can run a short two-week Dedicated POC with a single GPU pool and a simulated noisy tenant to demonstrate isolation and P99 behavior. We can instrument token-level tracing and per-route SLO dashboards for your team.

—Aditya
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
